apply-quiet.sql:
with open_requests as (
  select count(*)::integer as n, min(g.id) as first_id
    from public.agent_requests g
   where g.kind in ('sync', 'inbox_feedback') and g.state in ('queued', 'claimed')
), waiting as (
  select q.id
    from public.v_inbox_queue q
   where not (q.entity = 'agent_request' and q.course_id is null and q.ref like 'accept/%')
), held as (
  select count(*)::integer as n
    from public.inbox_apply_held_items() as h(id)
   where h.id in (select w.id from waiting w)
), login as (
  select count(*)::integer as n
    from public.attention_items i
   where i.kind = 'stack_must_confirm' and i.course_id is null and i.ref = 'sync-login-required'
     and i.field is null and i.state = 'open'
)
select (open_requests.n = 0 and (select count(*) from waiting) = 0 and login.n = 0) as ok,
       (open_requests.n > 0 or (select count(*) from waiting) > 0 or login.n > 0) as blocked,
       open_requests.n as requests_open, open_requests.first_id as first_open_request_id,
       (select count(*) from waiting)::integer as answers_waiting, held.n as answers_held, login.n as login_items_open
  from open_requests, held, login
apply-quiet.expect: One row. ok when no sync and no Inbox apply request is queued or claimed (of any age: the one-open rule of the apply requests holds an old one against a new press too), no answered Inbox row waits in v_inbox_queue but a test question of an acceptance run, and no sync-login-required item is open (the Blackboard login is alive; migration 091 raises that item when a sync closes login_required or the login watch fails, and sync_login_ok archives it when the login check passes). blocked when any of those counts is above 0: the run stops before anything is raised, and is repeated. A test question an earlier run left does not count: step 1 closes it. answers_held is how many of the waiting answers are held (inbox_apply_held_items), so the record says why a run was blocked: a press of Apply answers tries held answers, so they count too.

apply-idle.sql:
select (idle.n = 0) as ok, (idle.n > 0) as blocked, idle.n as requests_open, idle.first_id as first_open_request_id
  from (select count(*)::integer as n, min(g.id) as first_id
          from public.agent_requests g
         where g.kind = 'inbox_feedback' and g.state in ('queued', 'claimed')) idle
apply-idle.expect: One row. ok when no inbox_feedback request is queued or claimed. blocked when one is: stopping the apply service kills the CLI of a claimed request and closes it failed, which raises a notice in his Inbox, and a close of the run before it can file a follow-up. The host reads it before it stops the service, and the service is then left running.

questions-raised.sql:
with wanted(label, item_id, expected_kind) as (
  values ('confirm', $1::bigint, 'stack_must_confirm'),
         ('dismiss', $2::bigint, 'data_gap'),
         ('no' || 'te', $3::bigint, 'stack_must_confirm'),
         ('offline', $4::bigint, 'data_gap')
), judged as (
  select w.label, i.id, split_part(i.ref, '/', 2) as run_tag,
         (i.id is not null and i.kind = w.expected_kind and i.entity = 'agent_request' and i.course_id is null
          and i.raised_at >= $5::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'
          and split_part(i.ref, '/', 1) = 'accept' and split_part(i.ref, '/', 3) = w.label
          and split_part(i.ref, '/', 2) ~ '^[a-z0-9]{6,24}$') as shaped_and_raised,
         case w.label
           when 'confirm' then (i.resolved_at is not null and i.resolution->>'value' is not null and i.resolution_note is null)
           when 'dismiss' then (i.resolved_at is not null and i.resolution->>'dismissed' = 'true' and i.resolution_note is null)
           else true
         end as answered_right
    from wanted w
    left join public.attention_items i on i.id = w.item_id
)
select (count(j.id) = 4 and count(distinct j.id) = 4 and count(*) filter (where j.shaped_and_raised) = 4
        and count(*) filter (where j.answered_right) = 4 and count(distinct j.run_tag) = 1) as ok,
       count(j.id)::integer as items_found,
       (count(*) filter (where j.shaped_and_raised))::integer as shaped_and_raised_in_this_run,
       (count(*) filter (where j.answered_right and j.label in ('confirm', 'dismiss')))::integer as answers_right,
       count(distinct j.run_tag)::integer as run_tags
  from judged j
questions-raised.expect: One row. ok when the four items are four different rows, each shaped as inbox_accept_question raises one (entity agent_request, no course, ref accept/<run tag>/<label> with the label that item stands for, and the kind the label fixes: data_gap for dismiss and offline, stack_must_confirm for confirm and the third), each raised no earlier than 60 seconds before the run started, all four with one run tag, and the first two answered as step 1 says: confirm with a value in its answer and no reason, dismiss with the dismissed mark and no reason. What the third and fourth did afterwards is judged by later proofs. The third label is written in two pieces in the statement because the proofs' lint refuses that whole word anywhere in a statement.

sync-taken.sql:
with the_request as (
  select r.id, r.kind, r.state, r.created_at, r.claimed_at, r.claimed_by, r.finished_at
    from public.agent_requests r
   where r.id = $1::bigint
), login as (
  select exists (select 1
                   from public.attention_items i
                  where i.kind = 'stack_must_confirm' and i.course_id is null and i.ref = 'sync-login-required'
                    and i.field is null and i.raised_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as raised
)
select (q.kind = 'sync' and q.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'
        and q.claimed_by = 'sync-runner' and q.claimed_at is not null) as ok,
       (q.state = 'failed' and l.raised) as blocked,
       q.id as request_id, q.kind as request_kind, q.state as request_state, q.created_at, q.claimed_at, q.claimed_by, q.finished_at,
       (q.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as asked_in_this_run,
       (q.claimed_by = 'sync-runner' and q.claimed_at is not null) as taken_by_the_runner,
       l.raised as login_item_raised_in_this_run
  from the_request q
 cross join login l
sync-taken.expect: One row. ok when the request is a sync made no earlier than 60 seconds before the run started and the sync container took it (claimed_by sync-runner, with a claim time). blocked when the sync closed failed and a sync-login-required item was raised in this run: the sync closed login_required (migration 091 raises that item then) and the Blackboard login is dead, so the run is repeated. Whether the sync finished well is judged by the next step's proof.

recorded-after-sync.sql:
with the_sync as (
  select r.id, r.state
    from public.agent_requests r
   where r.id = $1::bigint and r.kind = 'sync'
), applies as (
  select v.*
    from public.v_inbox_apply_runs v
   where v.after_request = $1::bigint
), latest as (
  select a.* from applies a order by a.id desc limit 1
), first_one as (
  select i.id, i.decision->>'bucket' as bucket,
         (i.state = 'archived' and i.archived_by = 'inbox-apply request ' || l.id::text and i.entity = 'agent_request' and i.course_id is null and i.ref like 'accept/%' and i.raised_at >= $4::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as archived_by_it
    from public.attention_items i, latest l
   where i.id = $2::bigint
), second_one as (
  select i.id, i.decision->>'bucket' as bucket,
         (i.state = 'archived' and i.archived_by = 'inbox-apply request ' || l.id::text and i.entity = 'agent_request' and i.course_id is null and i.ref like 'accept/%' and i.raised_at >= $4::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as archived_by_it
    from public.attention_items i, latest l
   where i.id = $3::bigint
), facts as (
  select s.state as sync_state,
         (select count(*) from applies)::integer as apply_requests_naming_it,
         l.id as apply_request_id, l.filed_by as apply_filed_by, l.claimed_by as apply_claimed_by, l.state as apply_state,
         l.error_code as apply_error_code, l.claude_started as apply_claude_started, l.archived_count as apply_archived_count,
         (l.created_at >= $4::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as apply_filed_in_this_run,
         f.bucket as first_bucket, coalesce(f.archived_by_it, false) as first_archived_by_it,
         g.bucket as second_bucket, coalesce(g.archived_by_it, false) as second_archived_by_it,
         coalesce(s.state = 'done'
                  and (select count(*) from applies) = 1
                  and l.filed_by = 'sync' and l.claimed_by = 'inbox-apply-runner' and l.state = 'done' and l.error_code is null
                  and l.created_at >= $4::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'
                  and f.archived_by_it and f.bucket = 'recorded_elsewhere'
                  and g.archived_by_it and g.bucket = 'dismissed', false) as checks_pass,
         coalesce(l.error_code in ('daily_cap', 'usage_limit'), false) as met_a_limit,
         coalesce(s.state in ('queued', 'claimed') or l.state in ('queued', 'claimed'), false) as still_open
    from the_sync s
    left join latest l on true
    left join first_one f on true
    left join second_one g on true
)
select f.checks_pass as ok, (not f.checks_pass and (f.met_a_limit or f.still_open)) as blocked, f.*
  from facts f
recorded-after-sync.expect: One row. ok when the sync is done and exactly one inbox_feedback request names it (after_request), that request was filed by the sync (filed_by sync), taken by the apply worker (inbox-apply-runner), made in this run, and closed done with no error code, and the first question was archived by that request in bucket recorded_elsewhere and the second in bucket dismissed. blocked, not failed, when the checks did not pass and the apply request closed with the error daily_cap or usage_limit (the worker starts at most 12 runs a New York day, and the Claude plan has a limit), or the sync or the apply request is still queued or claimed when this is read (the watch of step 3 is limited, a slow run is not a fault): the run is repeated. The ids are the sandbox's pointers; this statement reads the rows and decides.

nothing-written.sql:
with found as (
  select i.id, (i.entity = 'agent_request' and i.course_id is null and i.ref like 'accept/%' and i.raised_at >= $3::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as this_runs_question
    from public.attention_items i
   where i.id in ($1::bigint, $2::bigint)
)
select (count(*) = 2 and count(*) filter (where f.this_runs_question) = 2
        and (select count(*) from public.inbox_apply_writes w where w.item_id in ($1::bigint, $2::bigint)) = 0) as ok,
       count(*)::integer as items_found,
       (count(*) filter (where f.this_runs_question))::integer as raised_in_this_run,
       (select count(*) from public.inbox_apply_writes w where w.item_id in ($1::bigint, $2::bigint))::integer as writes_logged
  from found f
nothing-written.expect: One row. ok when the two items are two different test questions raised in this run (entity agent_request, no course, an accept/ ref, raised no earlier than 60 seconds before the run started) and the write log (inbox_apply_writes) holds no row for either: the worker recorded them without changing any table.

applied-from-button.sql:
with the_request as (
  select v.*
    from public.v_inbox_apply_runs v
   where v.id = $1::bigint
), facts as (
  select r.id as request_id, r.state as request_state, r.filed_by as request_filed_by, r.claimed_by as request_claimed_by,
         r.claude_started as request_claude_started, r.error_code as request_error_code, r.finished_at as request_finished_at,
         (r.id > $3::bigint) as request_after_sync,
         (r.created_at >= $4::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as asked_in_this_run,
         coalesce(t.state = 'archived' and t.archived_by = 'inbox-apply request ' || r.id::text, false) as item_archived_by_it,
         coalesce(t.entity = 'agent_request' and t.course_id is null and t.ref like 'accept/%' and t.raised_at >= $4::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds', false) as item_is_this_runs_question,
         coalesce(t.resolution_note is not null, false) as item_had_a_reason,
         (select count(*) from public.inbox_apply_writes w where w.item_id = $2::bigint)::integer as writes_logged
    from the_request r
    left join public.attention_items t on t.id = $2::bigint
), judged as (
  select f.*,
         (f.request_state = 'done' and f.request_filed_by = 'button' and f.request_claimed_by = 'inbox-apply-runner'
          and f.request_claude_started and f.request_error_code is null and f.request_finished_at is not null
          and f.request_after_sync and f.asked_in_this_run
          and f.item_archived_by_it and f.item_is_this_runs_question and f.item_had_a_reason and f.writes_logged = 0) as checks_pass,
         coalesce(f.request_error_code in ('daily_cap', 'usage_limit'), false) as met_a_limit,
         f.request_state in ('queued', 'claimed') as still_open
    from facts f
)
select j.checks_pass as ok, (not j.checks_pass and (j.met_a_limit or j.still_open)) as blocked, j.*
  from judged j
applied-from-button.expect: One row. ok when the request was filed from the button (filed_by button: a press files a request with no trigger), made in this run and later than the sync's own request (its id is above the carried sync request's), taken by the apply worker, started Claude, and closed done with no error code; the third question (a test question of this run, answered with a reason) was archived by that request; and the write log holds no row for it. blocked, not failed, when the checks did not pass and the request closed with the error daily_cap or usage_limit, or is still queued or claimed when this is read (step 6 waits no longer than the operator can, and a Claude run may take up to 14 minutes): the run is repeated.

request-waiting.sql:
select (r.state = 'queued' and r.claimed_by is null and r.claimed_at is null and r.finished_at is null and r.error_code is null
        and r.filed_by = 'button' and r.created_at >= $3::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'
        and coalesce(t.state = 'dismissed' and t.entity = 'agent_request' and t.course_id is null and t.ref like 'accept/%' and t.raised_at >= $3::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds', false)) as ok,
       r.id as request_id, r.state as request_state, r.claimed_by as request_claimed_by, r.filed_by as request_filed_by,
       r.error_code as request_error_code, r.created_at,
       (r.created_at >= $3::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as asked_in_this_run,
       coalesce(t.state = 'dismissed' and t.entity = 'agent_request' and t.course_id is null and t.ref like 'accept/%' and t.raised_at >= $3::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds', false) as item_waiting,
       floor(extract(epoch from (now() - r.created_at)))::integer as waited_s
  from public.v_inbox_apply_runs r
  left join public.attention_items t on t.id = $2::bigint
 where r.id = $1::bigint
request-waiting.expect: One row. ok when the request was filed from the button in this run and is in the queue now (state queued, taken by nobody, not ended, no error code), and the fourth question, a test question of this run, is answered (dismissed) and not archived. It is read while the apply service is still stopped, so it shows that a press made while the worker is down waits and does not expire. waited_s is how long it has waited so far, by the database's clock.

request-taken-after.sql:
with facts as (
  select r.id as request_id, r.state as request_state, r.claimed_by as request_claimed_by, r.filed_by as request_filed_by,
         r.error_code as request_error_code,
         (r.created_at >= $3::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as asked_in_this_run,
         $4::integer as min_wait_s,
         floor(extract(epoch from (r.claimed_at - r.created_at)))::integer as waited_s,
         (r.claimed_at >= r.created_at + make_interval(secs => $4::integer)) as waited_long_enough,
         coalesce(t.state = 'archived' and t.archived_by = 'inbox-apply request ' || r.id::text, false) as item_archived_by_it,
         coalesce(t.entity = 'agent_request' and t.course_id is null and t.ref like 'accept/%' and t.raised_at >= $3::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds', false) as item_is_this_runs_question,
         t.decision->>'bucket' as bucket,
         (r.state = 'done' and r.error_code is null and r.filed_by = 'button' and r.claimed_by = 'inbox-apply-runner'
          and r.finished_at is not null) as request_done
    from public.v_inbox_apply_runs r
    left join public.attention_items t on t.id = $2::bigint
   where r.id = $1::bigint
)
select (f.request_done and f.asked_in_this_run and coalesce(f.waited_long_enough, false)
        and f.item_archived_by_it and f.item_is_this_runs_question and f.bucket = 'dismissed') as ok,
       (not (f.request_done and f.asked_in_this_run and coalesce(f.waited_long_enough, false)
             and f.item_archived_by_it and f.item_is_this_runs_question and f.bucket = 'dismissed')
        and (coalesce(f.request_error_code in ('daily_cap', 'usage_limit'), false) or f.request_state = 'claimed')) as blocked,
       f.*
  from facts f
request-taken-after.expect: One row. ok when the request was filed from the button in this run, was taken by the apply worker at least min_wait_s seconds after it was filed (both times are the database's own; no clock of a sandbox is compared), and closed done with no error code; and the fourth question (a test question of this run) was archived by that request in bucket dismissed. blocked, not failed, when the checks did not pass and the request closed with the error daily_cap or usage_limit, or the worker has taken it and has not closed it yet (state claimed: a slow run). A request still queued after the worker was started is not blocked: that is what the step tests, and it fails.

test-decisions-skipped.sql:
with wanted(item_id) as (
  values ($1::bigint), ($2::bigint), ($3::bigint), ($4::bigint)
), judged as (
  select i.id,
         coalesce(i.state = 'archived' and i.decision->>'schema' = 'inbox-decision/1' and i.decision_filed_at is not null
            and i.decision_filed->>'skipped' = 'true'
            and coalesce(jsonb_typeof(i.decision_filed->'note_path'), 'null') = 'null'
            and coalesce(jsonb_typeof(i.decision_filed->'log_path'), 'null') = 'null'
            and i.entity = 'agent_request' and i.course_id is null and i.ref like 'accept/%' and i.raised_at >= $5::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds', false) as skipped_with_no_note
    from wanted w
    left join public.attention_items i on i.id = w.item_id
)
select (count(j.id) = 4 and count(distinct j.id) = 4 and count(*) filter (where j.skipped_with_no_note) = 4) as ok,
       count(j.id)::integer as items_found,
       (count(*) filter (where j.skipped_with_no_note))::integer as skipped_with_no_note
  from judged j

transform-answers.sql:
with answers as (
  select ai.id, ai.applied_at,
         case when length(split_part(ai.ref, '/', 2)) between 1 and 18 and split_part(ai.ref, '/', 2) !~ '[^0-9]'
              then split_part(ai.ref, '/', 2)::bigint end as file_id,
         case when length(ai.resolution->>'session_id') between 1 and 18 and (ai.resolution->>'session_id') !~ '[^0-9]'
              then (ai.resolution->>'session_id')::bigint end as pick
    from public.attention_items ai
   where ai.kind = 'stack_must_confirm' and ai.entity = 'bb_file' and ai.field = 'session_id'
     and ai.ref ~ '^session_link/[0-9]'
     and ai.state in ('resolved', 'archived')
     and (ai.state <> 'archived' or ai.decision->>'closed_itself' is distinct from 'true')
), on_file as (
  select a.id, a.applied_at
    from answers a
    join public.bb_files f on f.id = a.file_id
   where f.superseded_by is null and f.session_id is not null and f.session_id = a.pick
), looked_at as (
  select ai.id, ai.ref, ai.state, ai.to_value, ai.decision
    from public.attention_items ai
   where ai.kind = 'stack_must_confirm' and ai.entity = 'bb_file' and ai.field = 'superseded_by'
     and ai.ref ~ '^supersede/[0-9]'
), reasked as (
  select o.id
    from looked_at o
   where o.state = 'open'
     and exists (select 1
                   from looked_at a
                  where a.ref = o.ref and a.state = 'archived' and a.decision->>'closed_itself' is distinct from 'true'
                    and a.to_value is not distinct from o.to_value)
)
select ((select count(*) from on_file f where f.applied_at is null) = 0 and (select count(*) from reasked) = 0) as ok,
       (select count(*) from on_file)::integer as session_answers_with_pick_on_file,
       (select count(*) from on_file f where f.applied_at is null)::integer as session_answers_unstamped,
       (select count(*) from on_file f where f.applied_at >= $1::timestamptz)::integer as session_answers_stamped_since_start,
       (select count(*) from looked_at)::integer as supersede_items_looked_at,
       (select count(*) from reasked)::integer as supersede_reasked
transform-answers.expect: One row, and the counts are in it. ok when no session answer whose pick its file now carries lacks the stamp (applied_at) and no supersede question is open beside an archived answer, one that did not close itself, for the same file and the same candidates. It passes on zero rows, which is why the record must say which counts were zero: session_answers_with_pick_on_file is how many session answers (resolved or archived, not self-closed) name the session their current file carries, session_answers_unstamped how many of those lack the stamp, session_answers_stamped_since_start how many were stamped at or after the run started, supersede_items_looked_at how many supersede questions exist, supersede_reasked how many are asked again. A count of zero is written not exercised, never passed.
